standard_prerequisites.name: Lifting a map between complexes out of a bounded above complex of finite free modules
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Derived Categories, Lemma \ref{derived-lemma-lift-map}, cited at proof lines 15934-15935
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the map between the two approximating complexes that makes the square commute in the derived category.

standard_prerequisites.name: The four and five lemmas for the comparison of long exact cohomology sequences
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Homology, Lemma \ref{homology-lemma-four-lemma} and Homology, Lemma \ref{homology-lemma-five-lemma}, cited at proof lines 15947-15948
standard_prerequisites.use: Convert the comparison map of triangles into the isomorphism and surjectivity statements on cohomology.

core_obligations: Choose an approximation of the first term by a bounded complex of finite free modules with the required cohomological behaviour (proof lines 15926-15931).
Truncate that complex so that it vanishes below degree m + 1 (proof lines 15931-15933).
Choose the analogous approximation of the second term and lift the map between the terms to a map of complexes (proof lines 15933-15939).
Observe that the cone of the lifted map is a bounded complex of finite free modules and maps to the third term, giving a morphism of distinguished triangles (proof lines 15940-15945).
Apply the four and five lemmas to conclude that the third term is m-pseudo-coherent, and obtain the remaining two statements by rotation (proof lines 15946-15962).
proof_roadmap: Take the cone and the morphism of triangles (proof lines 15940-15945).
difficulty_reason: The lemma records how m-pseudo-coherence behaves in a distinguished triangle: if the first term is one degree better and the second is m-pseudo-coherent then so is the third, and the two symmetric statements obtained by rotation. The proof of the first statement chooses bounded complexes of finite free modules mapping to the first two terms with the prescribed cohomological approximation, truncates the first one so that it lives in degrees at least m + 1, lifts the map between the two terms to a map between the chosen complexes using the lifting lemma for maps out of such approximations, and then observes that the cone of that map is again a bounded complex of finite free modules and maps to the third term compatibly, so that the four and five lemmas produce the required isomorphism and surjection on cohomology. The remaining statements are obtained by rotating the triangle.
